observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a moss-covered stone or concrete spout (shaped like a rough carved head or pipe elbow) protruding from the right, discharging a continuous clear water stream that falls into a dark pool. A thin sheet of water also runs off the top/right of the structure. The background is out-of-focus dried straw and earth. The pool surface shows a bright impact zone with white foam, scattered bubbles, concentric ripples, and a vertical shimmering reflection of the falling column.
visible_changes: The falling water column remains in the same position but its surface texture and edges flicker with turbulence from frame to frame (continuous flow, not starting or stopping).
The white splash/foam patch at the impact point and the distribution of bubbles on the pool surface change shape and intensity across the excerpt.
Ripples spread outward from the impact area and the vertical reflection of the stream wavers and breaks up.
The secondary water sheet on the right of the spout shimmers slightly.
The spout, background, and overall framing stay fixed; no object translation or camera pan/zoom is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: What feeds water into the spout and the full structure behind the right edge.
Events before t=0 and after the last frame (the flow is already ongoing at the crop start and continues at the end).
Whether the slight surface shimmer is from camera vibration or water motion alone.
uncertain_details: Exact material of the spout (mossy stone vs. concrete vs. wood).
Precise cause of minor frame-to-frame texture shifts in the stream (turbulence vs. compression artifacts).
